name: Elowyn Fearne
description:
ACorEx is as much an instrument as it is a performer in its own right, thus making my performances with it a sort of duet. There is a constant tension between it and myself. It pushes, and I push back. I pull, and it falls down a ravine of incoherence from which I have to drag it — screaming and kicking — back up. Each performance is a new discovery for everyone involved.

Of course, it is neither conscious nor intelligent, but it is also neither simple or stable. With some time and effort, patterns can be found, a rhythm achieved; Such moments are houses of cards, undone with the lightest touch.

ACorEx requires a collection of analysed audio files to function. This is too slow a process to not prepare in advance, and so form natural constraints for my improvisation through the finite soundscapes I set up to later pick from.
bio: Elowyn Fearne is an audio programmer, composer, and researcher. In 2025, she created ACorEx, a corpus-based concatenative synthesis instrument. Her compositions are a variety of electronic explorations with a stylistic interest in building rhythmic soundscapes of strange samples and evolving textures.
